Cache Overview

1. What is an Ignite Cache?
  • A cache is a named, distributed key-value store that lives in memory across the cluster;
  • It is the primary data structure in Ignite — all data storage goes through caches;
  • A cache is equivalent to a SQL table: the same data can be accessed via key-value API or SQL;
  • Caches are created at runtime (dynamically) or at startup (via configuration);
2. Creating Caches
  • Programmatically: 
    CacheConfiguration<Long, String> cfg = new CacheConfiguration<>("myCache");
cfg.setCacheMode(CacheMode.PARTITIONED);
cfg.setBackups(1);

IgniteCache<Long, String> cache = ignite.getOrCreateCache(cfg);
  • Via XML configuration: 
    <bean class="org.apache.ignite.configuration.IgniteConfiguration">
    <property name="cacheConfiguration">
        <bean class="org.apache.ignite.configuration.CacheConfiguration">
            <property name="name" value="myCache"/>
            <property name="cacheMode" value="PARTITIONED"/>
            <property name="backups" value="1"/>
        </bean>
    </property>
</bean>
  • Via SQL: 
    CREATE TABLE myTable (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR
) WITH "cache_name=myCache,template=partitioned,backups=1";
3. Destroying Caches
  • // Destroy the cache and delete all data
ignite.destroyCache("myCache");

// Or via SQL
DROP TABLE myTable;
  • Destroying a cache removes all data from all nodes — this is irreversible;
4. Cache Groups
  • By default each cache has its own set of partitions, which consumes memory for partition metadata;
  • Cache groups allow multiple caches to share the same set of partitions, reducing overhead;
  • Caches in the same group must have compatible configurations (same cache mode, same number of backups); 
    CacheConfiguration cfg1 = new CacheConfiguration("cache1");
cfg1.setGroupName("myGroup");

CacheConfiguration cfg2 = new CacheConfiguration("cache2");
cfg2.setGroupName("myGroup");
5. Atomicity Modes
Mode Description
TRANSACTIONAL Full ACID transactions across multiple keys and caches; supports pessimistic/optimistic concurrency;
ATOMIC (default) Each individual operation is atomic, but no multi-key transactions; better throughput for simple operations;
TRANSACTIONAL_SNAPSHOT MVCC-based transactions (experimental); provides snapshot isolation; 
CacheConfiguration cfg = new CacheConfiguration("myCache");
cfg.setAtomicityMode(CacheAtomicityMode.TRANSACTIONAL);
